scorecard.rationale: The Religa cross-sectional study linked higher olive-oil quantity to lower HADS anxiety outside Parkinson disease, with adjusted difference −1.86 points and 95% CI −3.54 to −0.18. Oil grade was unknown and the unadjusted item did not survive multiplicity correction. A cold-pressed rat-oil comparison had selected favorable behavior and inconclusive other maze outcomes. DieTBra did not isolate a favorable additive oil result and the overlapping TANDIM follow-up likewise provided no olive-oil-specific anxiety estimate. MEDI-PD is inconclusive for the oil. The newly identified hydroxytyrosol study concerns cultured retinal cells and contributes no symptom sign. The quantified human association retains a minimal easing tier and a direct matched Parkinson comparison remains open. The wine review names olive oil in a Mediterranean diet description without an independently assigned cold-pressed exposure or anxiety result. Olive oil appears in the earlier total-score food survey and in a Mediterranean pattern description. The surveys and review comparisons do not identify cold-pressed grade or an anxiety-specific effect.
